newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil panel to delay petroleum vote - lawmaker.
newsitem.headline: Brazil panel to delay petroleum vote - lawmaker.

text.p: A bill regulating the opening of Brazil's petroleum sector to private companies will probably be put to a vote in panel in the Chamber of Deputies Wednesday and not Tuesday as previously expected, a lawmaker said.

Deputy Eliseu Resende, who is in charge of drawing up the legislation, said Mines and Energy Minister Raimundo Brito, government leaders and other lawmakers were due to meet later Monday and Tuesday to discuss controversial points of the bill.

One question under discussion was a clause of the bill which would allow state oil and gas monopoly Petrobras to create subsidiaries and joint ventures without having to seek congressional approval on every occasion.
Left-wing opposition parties say that runs contrary to Brazil's constitution and might allow the government to sell off Petrobras assets without formally privatizing the company.
The parties have threatened to challenge the legislation in the courts if the clause is not removed.

Another important issue being studied was a proposed amendment to the bill which would allow the government to privatize Petrobras. The legislation in its current form obliges the government to maintain 50 percent plus one of Petrobras' voting shares.
Resende told reporters, however, he did not expect major changes to be made to his bill.

Brazil's Congress approved in 1995 a constitutional amendment that did away with Petrobras monopoly in several areas of the petroleum industry but has yet to come up with the enabing legislation to put the change into practice.
Resende's bill would allow privte companies to compete or go into partnership with Petrobras.
